sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca śatena niṣkaṃ gaṇitaṃ sahasreṇa ca saṃmitam yathā bahu pratīcchan hi pāpiṣṭhāṃ labhate gatim
english: Vasiṣṭha said: A gold coin counted by hundreds, reckoned by thousands — the man who accepts ever more of it surely wins the most sinful destiny.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca yat pṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ sarvaṃ tan nālam ekasya tasmād vidvāñ śamaṃ vrajet
english: Kaśyapa said: All the rice and barley, the gold, the cattle, and the women upon this earth — even all of it is not enough for one man; therefore let the wise go to tranquility.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca utpannasya ruroḥ śṛṅgaṃ vardhamānasya vardhate prārthanā puruṣasyeva tasya mātrā na vidyate
english: Bharadvāja said: As the horn of the ruru deer, once sprung up, keeps growing as the creature grows, so a man's craving grows; of it no measure can be found.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca na tal loke dravyam asti yal lokaṃ pratipūrayet samudrakalpaḥ puruṣo na kadā cana pūryate
english: Gautama said: There is no substance in the world that could fill the world; a man is like the ocean — he is never, ever filled.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca kāmaṃ kāmayamānasya yadā kāmaḥ samṛdhyate athainam aparaḥ kāmas tṛṣṇā vidhyati bāṇavat
english: Viśvāmitra said: When the desire of a man who desires some object is fulfilled, then yet another desire, a thirst, pierces him like an arrow.

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca pratigrahe saṃyamo vai tapo dhārayate dhruvam tad dhanaṃ brāhmaṇasyeha lubhyamānasya visravet
english: Jamadagni said: Restraint in accepting gifts is austerity; it surely upholds him firmly. That wealth of a brahmin who grows greedy here flows away and is lost.

sanskrit: arundhaty uvāca dharmārthaṃ saṃcayo yo vai dravyāṇāṃ pakṣasaṃmataḥ tapaḥsaṃcaya eveha viśiṣṭo dravyasaṃcayāt
english: Arundhatī said: Though the gathering of goods for the sake of dharma is approved by some, here the gathering of austerity is far superior to the gathering of goods.

sanskrit: gaṇḍovāca ugrād ito bhayād yasmād bibhyatīme mameśvarāḥ balīyāṃso durbalavad bibhemy aham ataḥ param
english: Gaṇḍā said: From that fierce peril for which these my masters, mighty though they are, tremble like the weak, I too tremble all the more from this time on.

sanskrit: paśusakha uvāca yad vai dharme paraṃ nāsti brāhmaṇās tad dhanaṃ viduḥ vinayārthaṃ suvidvāṃsam upāseyaṃ yathātatham
english: Paśusakha said: That beyond which there is nothing higher in dharma — that the brahmins know to be true wealth. For the sake of discipline I would duly wait upon a man of deep learning.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ kuśalaṃ saha dānāya tasmai yasya prajā imāḥ phalāny upadhiyuktāni ya evaṃ naḥ prayacchasi
english: The sages said: Well-being, together with the gift, to him whose subjects these are! But fruits laden with a hidden snare — such as these you offer us in this way.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktvā hemagarbhāṇi hitvā tāni phalāni te ṛṣayo jagmur anyatra sarva eva dhṛtavratāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus and cast aside those fruits stuffed with gold within, the sages, every one of them firm in their vows, went elsewhere.

sanskrit: mantriṇaḥ ūcuḥ upadhiṃ śaṅkamānās te hitvemāni phalāni vai tato 'nyenaiva gacchanti viditaṃ te 'stu pārthiva
english: The ministers said: Suspecting a hidden snare, they have cast these fruits aside and now go off by another route altogether. Let this be known to you, O king.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu bhṛtyais tair vṛṣādarbhiś cukopa ha teṣāṃ saṃpratikartuṃ ca sarveṣām agamad gṛham
english: Thus addressed by those servants, Vṛṣādarbhi grew enraged; and to take revenge upon them all, he went into his house.

sanskrit: sa gatvāhavanīye 'gnau tīvraṃ niyamam āsthitaḥ juhāva saṃskṛtāṃ mantrair ekaikām āhutiṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Going there, the king took up a severe observance and, in the consecrated fire, offered one by one the oblations sanctified with sacred formulas.

sanskrit: tasmād agneḥ samuttasthau kṛtyā lokabhayaṃkarī tasyā nāma vṛṣādarbhir yātudhānīty athākarot
english: Out of that fire there arose a Kṛtyā, a sorcery-fiend who struck terror into the world; and Vṛṣādarbhi gave her the name Yātudhānī.

sanskrit: sā kṛtyā kālarātrīva kṛtāñjalir upasthitā vṛṣādarbhiṃ narapatiṃ kiṃ karomīti cābravīt
english: That Kṛtyā, like Kālarātri the Night of Doom, stood before him with hands joined in reverence and said to King Vṛṣādarbhi, "What shall I do?"

sanskrit: vṛṣādarbhir uvāca ṛṣīṇāṃ gaccha saptānām arundhatyās tathaiva ca dāsībhartuś ca dāsyāś ca manasā nāma dhāraya
english: Vṛṣādarbhi said: Go to the seven sages, and to Arundhatī as well, and to the husband of the slave-woman and to the slave-woman herself; fix their names firmly in your mind.

sanskrit: jñātvā nāmāni caiteṣāṃ sarvān etān vināśaya vinaṣṭeṣu yathā svairaṃ gaccha yatrepsitaṃ tava
english: Once you have learned their names, destroy them all; and when they are destroyed, go freely as you please, wherever you wish.

sanskrit: sā tatheti pratiśrutya yātudhānī svarūpiṇī jagāma tad vanaṃ yatra vicerus te maharṣayaḥ
english: Promising "So be it," Yātudhānī, taking on a form of her own, went to that forest in which those great sages were wandering.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca athātripramukhā rājan vane tasmin maharṣayaḥ vyacaran bhakṣayanto vai mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Now, O king, the great sages led by Atri were wandering in that forest, living upon roots and fruits.

sanskrit: athāpaśyan supīnāṃsapāṇipādamukhodaram parivrajantaṃ sthūlāṅgaṃ parivrājaṃ śunaḥsakham
english: Then they saw a wandering mendicant, Śunaḥsakha, roaming about — a man of stout limbs, with well-fleshed shoulders, hands, feet, face, and belly.

sanskrit: arundhatī tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvāṅgopacitaṃ śubhā bhavitāro bhavanto vai naivam ity abravīd ṛṣīn
english: But the lovely Arundhatī, seeing him grown full in every limb, said to the sages, "You yourselves will surely come to be like this — yet it is not so."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākam agnihotram anirhutam sāyaṃ prātaś ca hotavyaṃ tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha said: This man does not, as we do, have an agnihotra left unoffered, to be made evening and morning; that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: atrir uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākaṃ kṣudhā vīryaṃ samāhatam kṛcchrādhītaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ ca tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Atri said: This man's vigor is not, as ours is, struck down by hunger, nor is what he learned with hardship now lost; that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākaṃ śaśvac chāstraṃ jaradgavaḥ alasaḥ kṣutparo mūrkhas tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra said: This man has not, as we do, the sacred lore ever upon him like an old ox at its yoke; he is idle, given over to hunger, a dullard — that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākaṃ bhaktam indhanam eva ca saṃcintya vārṣikaṃ kiṃ cit tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Jamadagni said: This man has not, as we do, any rainy-season store of food and firewood to fret over and lay by; that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākaṃ catvāraś ca sahodarāḥ dehi dehīti bhikṣanti tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Kaśyapa said: This man does not, as we do, have four brothers born of one womb who beg, "Give, give!"; that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākaṃ brahmabandhor acetasaḥ śoko bhāryāpavādena tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: This man has not, as has a witless wretch of a brahmin like us, grief from a wife's reproaches; that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca naitasyeha yathāsmākaṃ trikauśeyaṃ hi rāṅkavam ekaikaṃ vai trivārṣīyaṃ tena pīvāñ śunaḥsakhaḥ
english: Gautama said: This man has not, as we do, three woolen rāṅkava blankets, each one to last three years; that is why Śunaḥsakha is so plump.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha dṛṣṭvā parivrāṭ sa tān maharṣīñ śunaḥsakhaḥ abhigamya yathānyāyaṃ pāṇisparśam athācarat
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the wandering mendicant Śunaḥsakha, seeing those great sages, drew near and duly greeted them with a touch of the hand.

sanskrit: paricaryāṃ vane tāṃ tu kṣutpratīghātakārikām anyonyena nivedyātha prātiṣṭhanta sahaiva te
english: And telling one another of their forest livelihood, which served to ward off hunger, they then set out together.

sanskrit: ekaniścayakāryāś ca vyacaranta vanāni te ādadānāḥ samuddhṛtya mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: United in a single resolve and purpose, they roamed the woods, digging up and gathering roots and fruits.

sanskrit: kadā cid vicarantas te vṛkṣair aviralair vṛtām śucivāriprasannodāṃ dadṛśuḥ padminīṃ śubhām
english: Once, as they wandered, they came upon a lovely lotus pond, ringed by close-set trees, its water pure, bright, and clear.

sanskrit: bālādityavapuḥprakhyaiḥ puṣkarair upaśobhitām vaidūryavarṇasadṛśaiḥ padmapatrair athāvṛtām
english: It was adorned with blossoms shining like the body of the newly risen sun, and covered over with lotus leaves the color of beryl.

sanskrit: nānāvidhaiś ca vihagair jalaprakarasevibhiḥ ekadvārām anādeyāṃ sūpatīrthām akardamām
english: It was thronged with birds of many kinds that haunt the spreading waters, having but a single approach, no one to claim it, with fair landings and free of mud.

sanskrit: vṛṣādarbhiprayuktā tu kṛtyā vikṛtadarśanā yātudhānīti vikhyātā padminīṃ tām arakṣata
english: But the Kṛtyā set to her task by Vṛṣādarbhi, hideous of aspect and known as Yātudhānī, was guarding that lotus pond.

sanskrit: śunaḥsakhasahāyās tu bisārthaṃ te maharṣayaḥ padminīm abhijagmus te sarve kṛtyābhirakṣitām
english: With Śunaḥsakha for their companion, those great sages went up to the pond, seeking lotus stalks — all of them, to that pond guarded by the Kṛtyā.

sanskrit: tatas te yātudhānīṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtadarśanām sthitāṃ kamalinītīre kṛtyām ūcur maharṣayaḥ
english: Then the great sages, seeing that Yātudhānī, the Kṛtyā of hideous aspect, standing on the bank of the lotus pond, spoke to her.

sanskrit: ekā tiṣṭhasi kā nu tvaṃ kasyārthe kiṃ prayojanam padminītīram āśritya brūhi tvaṃ kiṃ cikīrṣasi
english: You stand here alone — who indeed are you? For whose sake, and with what purpose? Keeping to the bank of the lotus pond, tell us, what is it you mean to do?

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca yāsmi sāsmy anuyogo me na kartavyaḥ kathaṃ cana ārakṣiṇīṃ māṃ padminyā vitta sarve tapodhanāḥ
english: Yātudhānī said: I am whoever I am; no questioning of me is to be made, by any means. Know me, all you whose wealth is austerity, to be the guardian of this pond.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ sarva eva kṣudhārtāḥ sma na cānyat kiṃ cid asti naḥ bhavatyāḥ saṃmate sarve gṛhṇīmahi bisāny uta
english: The sages said: We are all tormented by hunger, and we have nothing else at all. So with your leave, we shall every one of us gather the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca samayena bisānīto gṛhṇīdhvaṃ kāmakārataḥ ekaiko nāma me proktvā tato gṛhṇīta māciram
english: Yātudhānī said: Take the lotus stalks from here on a condition, as you please: let each one of you first declare his name to me, and then gather them without delay.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vijñāya yātudhānīṃ tāṃ kṛtyām ṛṣivadhaiṣiṇīm atriḥ kṣudhāparītātmā tato vacanam abravīt
english: Bhīṣma said: Recognizing that Yātudhānī to be a Kṛtyā bent on the sages' destruction, Atri, his very self overwhelmed by hunger, then spoke these words.

sanskrit: arātrir atreḥ sā rātrir yāṃ nādhīte trir adya vai arātrir atrir ity eva nāma me viddhi śobhane
english: "A-rātri" is the night that for Atri is no-night, the night he does not study thrice in a day; therefore, fair one, know my name to be Atri, the "no-night."

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca yathodāhṛtam etat te mayi nāma mahāmune durdhāryam etan manasā gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This name of yours, great sage, as you have explained it to me, is hard to hold in the mind; go on, then — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca vasiṣṭho 'smi variṣṭho 'smi vase vāsaṃ gṛheṣv api variṣṭhatvāc ca vāsāc ca vasiṣṭha iti viddhi mām
english: Vasiṣṭha said: I am Vasiṣṭha, I am the most excellent (variṣṭha); I dwell (vase) even in houses my dwelling (vāsam). From being most excellent and from dwelling, know me as Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāmanairuktam etat te duḥkhavyābhāṣitākṣaram naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This etymology of your name has syllables hard to pronounce; it cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca kulaṃ kulaṃ ca kupapaḥ kupayaḥ kaśyapo dvijaḥ kāśyaḥ kāśanikāśatvād etan me nāma dhāraya
english: Kaśyapa said: "Lineage upon lineage," a guardian of the wicked, a protector — Kaśyapa the twice-born, of Kāśi, from his resemblance to a shining radiance (kāśa): hold this name of mine.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca yathodāhṛtam etat te mayi nāma mahāmune durdhāryam etan manasā gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This name of yours, great sage, as you have explained it to me, is hard to hold in the mind; go on, then — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca bhare sutān bhare śiṣyān bhare devān bhare dvijān bhare bhāryām anavyājo bharadvājo 'smi śobhane
english: Bharadvāja said: I support (bhare) my sons, I support my pupils, I support the gods, I support the twice-born, I support my wife, doing so without pretense — I am Bharadvāja, the upholder, O fair one.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāmanairuktam etat te duḥkhavyābhāṣitākṣaram naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This etymology of your name has syllables hard to pronounce; it cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca godamo damago 'dhūmo damo durdarśanaś ca te viddhi māṃ gautamaṃ kṛtye yātudhāni nibodha me
english: Gautama said: "Tamer of cattle," "tamer-goer," the smokeless one, restraint, the one hard to look upon — know me, O Kṛtyā, as Gautama; mark me well, Yātudhānī.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca yathodāhṛtam etat te mayi nāma mahāmune naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This name of yours, great sage, as you have explained it to me, cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca viśvedevāś ca me mitraṃ mitram asmi gavāṃ tathā viśvāmitram iti khyātaṃ yātudhāni nibodha me
english: Viśvāmitra said: The All-Gods (Viśvedevas) are my friends, and I too am a friend (mitra) to the cattle; mark me, O Yātudhānī, renowned as Viśvāmitra, friend of all.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāmanairuktam etat te duḥkhavyābhāṣitākṣaram naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This etymology of your name has syllables hard to pronounce; it cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: jamadagnir uvāca jājamadyajajā nāma mṛjā māha jijāyiṣe jamadagnir iti khyātam ato māṃ viddhi śobhane
english: Jamadagni said: Born of sacrifice and offering, by name "the purifier," she said, "you wish to be born" — renowned as Jamadagni; from this know me, O fair one.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca yathodāhṛtam etat te mayi nāma mahāmune naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This name of yours, great sage, as you have explained it to me, cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: arundhaty uvāca dharāṃ dharitrīṃ vasudhāṃ bhartus tiṣṭhāmy anantaram mano 'nurundhatī bhartur iti māṃ viddhy arundhatīm
english: Arundhatī said: Like the earth, the sustainer, the bearer of wealth, I stand ever close behind my husband, holding my mind faithful to him (anurundhatī) — by this know me as Arundhatī.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāmanairuktam etat te duḥkhavyābhāṣitākṣaram naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This etymology of your name has syllables hard to pronounce; it cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: gaṇḍovāca gaṇḍaṃ gaṇḍaṃ gatavatī gaṇḍagaṇḍeti saṃjñitā gaṇḍagaṇḍeva gaṇḍeti viddhi mānalasaṃbhave
english: Gaṇḍā said: Going cheek by cheek (gaṇḍa by gaṇḍa), I am called Gaṇḍa-gaṇḍā; know me as Gaṇḍā, as it were "cheek upon cheek," O daughter of fire.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāmanairuktam etat te duḥkhavyābhāṣitākṣaram naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This etymology of your name has syllables hard to pronounce; it cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: paśusakha uvāca sakhā sakhe yaḥ sakhyeyaḥ paśūnāṃ ca sakhā sadā gauṇaṃ paśusakhety evaṃ viddhi mām agnisaṃbhave
english: Paśusakha said: A friend, in friendship, one fit to be befriended, and ever a friend (sakhā) to the cattle (paśus) — by this secondary derivation know me thus as Paśusakha, O you born of fire.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāmanairuktam etat te duḥkhavyābhāṣitākṣaram naitad dhārayituṃ śakyaṃ gacchāvatara padminīm
english: Yātudhānī said: This etymology of your name has syllables hard to pronounce; it cannot be held in mind. Go on — go down into the pond.

sanskrit: śunaḥsakha uvāca ebhir uktaṃ yathā nāma nāhaṃ vaktum ihotsahe śunaḥsakhasakhāyaṃ māṃ yātudhāny upadhāraya
english: Śunaḥsakha said: A name such as these have spoken I do not care to utter here; mark me, O Yātudhānī, as the companion of Śunaḥsakha, the dog's friend.

sanskrit: yātudhāny uvāca nāma te 'vyaktam uktaṃ vai vākyaṃ saṃdigdhayā girā tasmāt sakṛd idānīṃ tvaṃ brūhi yan nāma te dvija
english: Yātudhānī said: Your name has been spoken indistinctly, in words of doubtful sound; so now, O twice-born, tell me once and clearly what your name is.

sanskrit: śunaḥsakha uvāca sakṛd uktaṃ mayā nāma na gṛhītaṃ yadā tvayā tasmāt tridaṇḍābhihatā gaccha bhasmeti māciram
english: Śunaḥsakha said: My name was uttered once, and since you did not grasp it, therefore, struck down by the triple staff, go to ashes without delay!

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sā brahmadaṇḍakalpena tena mūrdhni hatā tadā kṛtyā papāta medinyāṃ bhasmasāc ca jagāma ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Struck then upon the head by that staff, which was like the rod of Brahmā, the Kṛtyā fell to the earth and was reduced to ashes.

sanskrit: śunaḥsakhaś ca hatvā tāṃ yātudhānīṃ mahābalām bhuvi tridaṇḍaṃ viṣṭabhya śādvale samupāviśat
english: And Śunaḥsakha, having slain that mighty Yātudhānī, planted his triple staff in the ground and sat down upon the grassy turf.

sanskrit: tatas te munayaḥ sarve puṣkarāṇi bisāni ca yathākāmam upādāya samuttasthur mudānvitāḥ
english: Then all the sages, taking lotus blossoms and stalks as they pleased, rose up filled with joy.

sanskrit: śrameṇa mahatā yuktās te bisāni kalāpaśaḥ tīre nikṣipya padminyās tarpaṇaṃ cakrur ambhasā
english: Wearied with great toil, they laid the lotus stalks in bundles on the bank of the pond and made the water-offering with its waters.

sanskrit: athotthāya jalāt tasmāt sarve te vai samāgaman nāpaśyaṃś cāpi te tāni bisāni puruṣarṣabha
english: Then, rising up from that water, they all came together — and yet, O bull among men, they could not see those lotus stalks.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ kena kṣudhābhibhūtānām asmākaṃ pāpakarmaṇā nṛśaṃsenāpanītāni bisāny āhārakāṅkṣiṇām
english: The sages said: By what evildoer, what cruel wretch, have the lotus stalks been carried off from us — overcome by hunger and longing for food?

sanskrit: te śaṅkamānās tv anyonyaṃ papracchur dvijasattamāḥ ta ūcuḥ śapathaṃ sarve kurma ity arikarśana
english: Suspecting one another, those best of the twice-born questioned each other; and they all said, "Let us swear an oath," O scourge of your foes.

sanskrit: ta uktvā bāḍham ity eva sarva eva śunaḥsakham kṣudhārtāḥ supariśrāntāḥ śapathāyopacakramuḥ
english: Saying "Yes, indeed," all of them, together with Śunaḥsakha, tormented by hunger and utterly worn out, set about taking the oath.

sanskrit: atrir uvāca sa gāṃ spṛśatu pādena sūryaṃ ca pratimehatu anadhyāyeṣv adhīyīta bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Atri said: Let him touch a cow with his foot and pass water facing the sun, and study on the forbidden days — whoever it is that has stolen the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca anadhyāyaparo loke śunaḥ sa parikarṣatu parivrāṭ kāmavṛtto 'stu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Let him in this world be one who shuns sacred study and instead drags a dog about, a wandering mendicant given to his own desires — whoever it is that has stolen the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: śaraṇāgataṃ hantu mitraṃ svasutāṃ copajīvatu arthān kāṅkṣatu kīnāśād bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Let him slay one who has come to him for refuge, betray a friend, live off his own daughter, and crave wealth from a miser — whoever it is that has stolen the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: kaśyapa uvāca sarvatra sarvaṃ paṇatu nyāsalopaṃ karotu ca kūṭasākṣitvam abhyetu bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Kaśyapa said: Let him gamble everything away on everything, embezzle what is left in trust, and become a false witness — whoever it is that has stolen the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: vṛthāmāṃsaṃ samaśnātu vṛthādānaṃ karotu ca yātu striyaṃ divā caiva bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Let him eat meat offered in vain, make gifts in vain, and go in to a woman by day — whoever it is that has stolen the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca nṛśaṃsas tyaktadharmāstu strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca brāhmaṇaṃ cāpi jayatāṃ bisastainyaṃ karoti yaḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: Let him be cruel and abandoned by dharma toward women, kinsmen, and cattle, and let him even win out over a brahmin — whoever it is that has stolen the lotus stalks.
